title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



I am a part designer, part climate detective, always chasing the question of how water, land, and cities can get along better. Trained as an architect, now deep in the world of landscape urbanism. Currently sharpening my data chops, because the future of design, she’d say, needs both a good eye and good numbers.Off the clock, she’s training for her next marathon, hunting down the best food in whatever city she’s in, and never says no to a good beer (❁´◡`❁)

title: About Me
text:
Master student of Urban Spatial Analytics (MUSA) at the Weitzman School of Design, University of Pennsylvania, taking my practice deeper into the data behind the design.
Trained as both an architect and urbanist, I transform climate science into adaptive urban strategies that treat environmental change not as a threat, but as a catalyst for resilience. I design with water flow, seasonal flooding, and ecological shift, not against them.
My work spans projected climate scenarios, participatory planning, and interventions like floodable landscapes and climate-adaptive urban foodscapes. Always at the intersection of environmental data, policy, and design, and always in pursuit of strategies that are equitable, not just forward-thinking.
